sections.position: Administrative Assistant @ TRACTORES Y MAQUINARIA REAL
sections.bio:
I build AI production systems for brands that need commercial content without traditional costs.
Not just generating images; engineering repeatable workflows that turn creative direction into scalable assets. Product visualization, brand campaigns, sports media.

My background in Industrial Engineering shapes how I approach creative work: as a controllable, optimizable process rather than hoping AI “gets it.”

What I do:
Transform vague prompts into reliable commercial output by combining tools strategically (Kling, Nano Banana Pro, Midjourney, Veo, etc).

Build creative supply chains, from concept to finished asset, that brands can actually use.
Bridge technical execution and artistic direction so taste becomes the bottleneck, not tooling.
Working with brands ready to ship AI content, not just experiment with it.

posts.text:
Most companies create content once and call it global.

But a video in English isn't a global video. It's an English video.

The brands that actually win in multiple markets aren't creating more content. They're making the same content work everywhere.

That's the problem Synthesia's video translator solves.

→ Translate any video into 130+ languages in minutes
→ Lip sync that actually matches, not dubbed audio over wrong mouth movements
→ Original speaker's voice preserved, not replaced
→ Upload any video or pull directly from a YouTube link
→ One player that serves every language version automatically

Traditional localization means hiring translators, voice actors, and an editor to resync everything. Minimum 2-3 weeks. Minimum several thousand dollars per language.

Most companies skip it. They post in English and wonder why their European or Latin American markets don't convert.

The content isn't the problem. The language is.

If you're running marketing across multiple countries right now and you're not localizing your video content, you're leaving a massive amount of reach on the table.

Comment "TRANSLATE" and I'll send you the link.

The death of location shoots.

But nobody in the industry wants to talk about it.

A location shoot in Europe runs you $15,000 minimum. Flights, crew, permits, accommodation, equipment. And that's before you've shot a single frame.
I did Norway from my desk in Mexico.

Same result. Different invoice.

AI video generation just made geography optional for commercial production. The client doesn't care where you shot it. They care if it looks right. If the light hits correctly. If the talent belongs in the environment.

That's a craft problem. Not a location problem.

Most production companies are still selling the logistics. The travel. The crew days. The location fees. That's where their margin lives.

That margin is gone.

The brands that figure this out first are going to cut production budgets in half and reinvest in more content, more formats, more markets.

The ones that don't will keep paying $15k for what I just did from my apartment.

Which industry do you think gets disrupted by this first?

I saw my work on a billboard yesterday.

SoniGas. Mazatlán. AI-produced commercial.

This is what the workflow looks like when it works:

→ Concept developed with AI image generation
→ Motion added in Kling/Seedance
→ Final polish in Photoshop
→ Delivered as a broadcast-ready ad

No traditional production crew. No location shoot. No six-figure budget.

I have capacity this month.

Been heads down building AI visual pipelines, spec campaigns, and affiliate content. But I’m open to jumping into something different.

If you’re working on a project and need someone who thinks in systems and executes fast, I’m available.

Industrial engineer. AI creative director. I figure things out.

DM me what you’re building and let’s see if we can work together.
